text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak parliament will re-open on March 12 an extraordinary session, interrupted last December, to discuss direct presidential elections and unspecified changes to the constitution.
- The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) is considering demanding inclusion of a law halting bank privatisation in the forthcoming extraordinary parliamentary session.
- Opposition parties on Tuesday handed a petition calling for a referendum on direct presidential elections to President Michal Kovac. Kovac must set the date for the referendum within 30 days.

- The National Property Funds (NPF) of the Czech and Slovak Republics, the countries' privatisation agencies, have signed an agreement on settling the privatisation disputes arising form the split of the two republics in 1993. The Czech NPF said the treaty will allow completion of privatisation of 64 companies, worth some 1.4 billion crowns.

- The Czech and Slovak Prime Ministers, Vaclav Klaus and Vladimir Meciar, are expected to discuss problems linked with exchange of shares held by both countries' NPFs in large commercial banks. The Slovak NPF holds a stake in the Czech Komercni Banka and the Czech NPF controls the Slovak VUB Bank.
- The Slovak bank Ludova Banka, majority-owned by the Austrian Osterreichische Volksbanken AG, posted a 1996 gross profit of around 113 million.
- Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft has lowered prices of its motor fuels for wholesalers, but the company does not expect the decrease to pull retail prices down in the near future.

PRAVDA - The Slovak government said one of the ways to curb the widening foreign trade deficit could be an increase in energy prices, arguing this could lead to lower energy consumption and subsequently to lower oil imports.
- Bilateral Slovak-Ukrainian talks this Thursday are expected to discuss the completion of an iron ore mining and processing complex at Dolinska, Ukraine.
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - The Slovak government approved a visa-free travel agreement with Israel. The treaty have yet to be approved by both parliaments.
